WAL-CLM-RARE-000238.answer_short: Wallach lists spinal cord demyelination, progressive neuropathy (nerve damage), and pernicious anemia as the common diseases of vitamin B12 deficiency.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000036.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000036.question: What are the signs of vitamin B2 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000036.answer_short: Wallach's signs of riboflavin (B2) deficiency include cracks at the corners of the mouth and nostrils, angular stomatitis, seborrheic dermatitis of the nasal folds, sore burning lips, mouth and tongue, geographic and magenta tongue, light sensitivity, tearing, bloodshot cornea, anemia, and neuropathy.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000113.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000113.question: How much vitamin B2 does Wallach recommend daily?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000113.answer_short: In his Epigenetics daily multiple, Wallach gives vitamin B2 (riboflavin) a daily range of 10 to 50 mg.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000234.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-RARE-000234.question: What diseases are caused by vitamin B2 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000234.answer_short: Wallach's common diseases of riboflavin (B2) deficiency include sore burning lips, mouth and tongue, erosions and swelling of the tongue (geographic tongue), magenta tongue, light sensitivity, excess tearing, cracked lips and mouth corners, angular stomatitis, seborrheic dermatitis of the nasal folds, bloodshot cornea, anemia, and neuropathy.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000037.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000037.question: What are the signs of vitamin B3 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000037.answer_short: Wallach ties niacin (B3) deficiency to pellagra and its 'three Ds' (diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia), plus retardation, muscular weakness, loss of appetite, 'beef tongue,' skin pigmentation, and a scaly, itchy dermatitis.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000114.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000114.question: How much vitamin B3 does Wallach recommend daily?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000114.answer_short: In his Epigenetics daily multiple, Wallach gives vitamin B3 (niacin) a daily range of 10 to 100 mg.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000019.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-LETS-000019.question: What are the symptoms of niacin deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000019.answer_short: Wallach's signs of niacin (B3) deficiency include anorexia and nausea, canker sores, confusion, depression, dermatitis, diarrhea, crying jags and emotional lability, fatigue, bad breath, headache, indigestion, insomnia, irritability, limb pains, memory loss, muscular weakness, and skin eruptions with eczema.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000020.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-LETS-000020.question: What are the signs of too much niacin?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000020.answer_short: Wallach lists the signs of niacin (B3) excess as the characteristic niacin 'flush' (skin flushing) and liver impairment.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000235.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-RARE-000235.question: What diseases does vitamin B3 deficiency cause?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000235.answer_short: Wallach's common diseases of niacin (B3) deficiency include pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia and retardation), muscular weakness, loss of appetite, sore 'beef tongue,' darkened skin pigmentation, and scaly dermatitis.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000038.subject: vitamin-b5
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000038.question: What are the signs of vitamin B5 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000038.answer_short: Wallach ties pantothenic acid (B5) deficiency to dermatitis, burning feet, muscle cramps, loss of appetite, anemia, a quarrelsome and sullen attitude, depression, insomnia, a depressed immune system, rapid heartbeat, fainting, and gastrointestinal distress.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000236.subject: vitamin-b5
WAL-CLM-RARE-000236.question: What diseases does vitamin B5 deficiency cause?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000236.answer_short: Wallach's common diseases of pantothenic acid (B5) deficiency include dermatitis, burning of the feet, loss of appetite, quarrelsomeness, sullenness, depression, rapid heartbeat, fainting, and indigestion.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000039.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000039.question: What are the signs of vitamin B6 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000039.answer_short: Wallach's signs of pyridoxine (B6) deficiency include depression and mental confusion, inflammation and lesions of the oral mucous membranes, nausea, vomiting, PMS, seborrheic dermatitis, carpal tunnel syndrome, TMJ problems, peripheral neuritis, ataxia, head tics (Tourette's syndrome), and seizures.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000108.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000108.question: Can vitamin B6 deficiency cause carpal tunnel syndrome?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000108.answer_short: A second cluster of B6 deficiency signs Wallach lists includes PMS, seborrheic dermatitis, itchy scaly skin, oral mucous membrane lesions, carpal tunnel syndrome, TMJ dysfunction, peripheral neuritis, ataxia, hyperirritability, head tics (Tourette's syndrome), and seizures or convulsions.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000152.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000152.question: What is potassium and what does it do in the body?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000152.answer_short: Wallach describes potassium as an essential mineral and the main positive ion inside cells, driving many enzyme and electrochemical functions, and making up about five percent of the body's total mineral content.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000153.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000153.question: How do potassium and sodium work together in the body?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000153.answer_short: Wallach explains that potassium and sodium together maintain the body's water balance, osmotic equilibrium, and acid-base balance, while potassium works with calcium to regulate nerve and muscle activity.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000154.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000154.question: How much potassium do you need each day?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000154.answer_short: Wallach says potassium is easily absorbed but barely stored, with about 90 percent excreted in the urine, so it needs a large daily intake of 5,000 mg.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000155.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000155.question: What are the signs of low potassium?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000155.answer_short: Wallach says low potassium first shows as muscular weakness and mental apathy, with its most serious form being hypokalemic cardiac failure, and that losses climb quickly with diuretics, heavy sweating, vomiting, or diarrhea.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000156.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000156.question: What makes you lose potassium?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000156.answer_short: Wallach warns that diuretics and fluid losses from colds, flu, exercise, vomiting, and diarrhea speed up the loss of all minerals, including potassium.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000006.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000006.question: What causes age spots and liver spots?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000006.answer_short: Wallach reads 'liver spots' or 'age spots' as an early outward sign of selenium deficiency and only the visible tip of ceroid lipofuscin deposits he says build up throughout the organs and sharply raise the risk of cancer, Alzheimer's, and heart disease.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000029.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000029.question: How does selenium work as an antioxidant?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000029.answer_short: Wallach calls selenium the most efficient antioxidant, working through the glutathione peroxidase enzyme system to keep body fats from going rancid.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000030.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000030.question: Is vegetable oil bad for your heart?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000030.answer_short: Wallach says that eating a lot of vegetable oil while low in selenium is the quickest route to a heart attack and cancer.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000071.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000071.question: Can selenium prevent muscular dystrophy?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000071.answer_short: Wallach says selenium prevents muscular dystrophy in all its forms, and that a preconception woman's selenium level matters for both maintaining pregnancy and preventing muscular dystrophy.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000004.subject: cystic_fibrosis
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000004.question: Is cystic fibrosis caused by a selenium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000004.answer_short: Wallach holds that cystic fibrosis is a nutritional deficiency of the trace mineral selenium rather than a purely genetic disease, drawn from his 1977 discovery of the lesions in a selenium-deficient monkey, and says it can be prevented, reversed, and cured with supplemental selenium.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000006.subject: cardiomyopathy
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000006.question: What causes sudden cardiac death in athletes?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000006.answer_short: Wallach holds that hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, including the sudden cardiac death of athletes, is Keshan disease caused by a simple selenium deficiency, and that a complete 90-nutrient program with extra selenium is protective.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000136.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000136.question: How much selenium should you take daily?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000136.answer_short: In his Epigenetics daily mineral recommendations, per 100 lb of body weight, Wallach gives selenium a range of 100 to 200 mcg a day.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000011.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000011.question: Can selenium deficiency cause prostate cancer?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000011.answer_short: Wallach links selenium deficiency to prostate cancer, using Linus Pauling — who downplayed minerals and died of prostate cancer at 94 — as his example.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000211.subject: keshan_disease
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000211.question: What causes Keshan disease?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000211.answer_short: Wallach attributes Keshan disease, observed in Keshan Province, China, to a selenium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000212.subject: cardiomyopathy
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000212.question: What causes cardiomyopathy?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000212.answer_short: Wallach attributes cardiomyopathy, which he identifies as Keshan disease, to a selenium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000030.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000030.question: What are the signs of selenium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000030.answer_short: Wallach lists the signs of selenium deficiency as cataracts, increased cancer risk, cystic fibrosis, growth retardation, heart attack, impaired immunity, Keshan disease, muscular dystrophy, pancreatic atrophy and fibrosis, liver cirrhosis, and sterility in males.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000031.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000031.question: What are the signs of too much selenium?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000031.answer_short: Wallach warns that selenium is toxic in excess, with tell-tale signs of hair loss, arthritis, brittle nails, garlic breath, a metallic taste, and kidney and liver dysfunction.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000197.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000197.question: Can selenium help prevent or treat cancer?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000197.answer_short: Wallach describes selenium as intensively studied for cancer prevention and therapy, considers 1,000 to 3,000 mcg a day the proper therapy dose, and notes plant-derived colloidal selenium is 98 percent absorbable.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000004.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000004.question: How did Wallach discover selenium's role in cystic fibrosis?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000004.answer_short: Wallach discovered the trace mineral selenium's pivotal role in the cause and prevention of cystic fibrosis while working as a research veterinary pathologist.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000048.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000048.question: Can selenium prevent Keshan disease?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000048.answer_short: Wallach cites a Chinese trial in which children given 1 mg of sodium selenite three times a week saw Keshan disease fall from 13 to 1 per 1,000 over three years, while the placebo group stayed at 13 per 1,000.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000050.subject: muscular_dystrophy
WAL-CLM-RARE-000050.question: Is muscular dystrophy caused by a selenium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000050.answer_short: Wallach holds that muscular dystrophy is a preventable selenium-deficiency disease, with its named forms merely classified by which muscle group is affected first, and notes the veterinary industry wiped out white muscle disease with simple selenium supplementation.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000084.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000084.question: Does selenium protect against mercury poisoning?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000084.answer_short: Wallach notes that minerals can neutralize the toxic effects of other minerals, with selenium a specific antidote for mercury poisoning and calcium for lead.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000225.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000225.question: How does selenium keep body fats from going rancid?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000225.answer_short: Wallach describes selenium as the most efficient antioxidant, acting in the glutathione peroxidase system to stop lipids from peroxidizing and keep body fats from going rancid, with the brown 'age spots' being that peroxidized lipid, ceroid lipofuscin.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000226.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000226.question: How does selenium protect cell membranes?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000226.answer_short: Wallach explains that selenium protects the bi-lipid-layer membranes of cells and organelles from oxidative damage; in a selenium-deficient monkey liver, the inner mitochondrial membrane collapses into a nonfunctioning crystalloid seen as 'age pigment.'

WAL-CLM-RARE-000227.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000227.question: What health problems does selenium deficiency cause in adults?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000227.answer_short: Wallach lists the conditions selenium deficiency produces in adults, including reduced immunity, anemia, infertility, age spots, muscle weakness, multiple sclerosis, ALS, Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, irregular heartbeat, cardiomyopathy, liver cirrhosis, cataracts, and cancer.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000269.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000269.question: What diseases are caused by a selenium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000269.answer_short: Wallach lists diseases of selenium deficiency including HIV/AIDS, anemia, age spots, fatigue, muscle weakness, scoliosis, muscular dystrophy, congenital cystic fibrosis, cardiomyopathy (Keshan disease), multiple sclerosis, heart palpitations, and liver cirrhosis.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000270.subject: selenium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000270.question: What diseases does selenium deficiency cause?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000270.answer_short: Wallach continues the list of selenium-deficiency diseases with pancreatitis, pancreatic atrophy, ALS, Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, adrenoleukodystrophy, infertility, low birth weight, high infant mortality, SIDS, cancer, clinical AIDS, and sickle cell anemia.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000306.subject: cancer
WAL-CLM-RARE-000306.question: What causes cancer according to Wallach?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000306.answer_short: Wallach attributes cancer to a selenium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000309.subject: cardiomyopathy
WAL-CLM-RARE-000309.question: What causes cardiomyopathy?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000309.answer_short: Wallach attributes cardiomyopathy to a selenium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000310.subject: cataracts
WAL-CLM-RARE-000310.question: What causes cataracts?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000310.answer_short: Wallach attributes cataracts to a selenium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000455.subject: gmo_foods
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000455.question: Does Wallach recommend eating non-GMO food?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000455.answer_short: Yes — Wallach lists consuming and stockpiling organic, non-GMO, fresh foods among his core principles for maximizing health and longevity.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000456.subject: emory_university
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000456.question: Where did Wallach discover cystic fibrosis?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000456.answer_short: At Emory University's Yerkes Primate Research Center, Wallach discovered the first non-human case of cystic fibrosis — in a young rhesus monkey in 1977.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000457.subject: emory_university
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000457.question: Was Wallach wrongly fired from Emory University?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000457.answer_short: Yes -- when Wallach announced that cystic fibrosis was not genetic but a congenital selenium deficiency, Emory's Yerkes facility summarily terminated him in April 1978 without any chance to defend his findings. Word of the firing by Emory and the NIH then cost him a new St. Louis University post before he had even moved into his offices.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000458.subject: twenty_thousand_autopsies
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000458.question: What did Wallach's autopsies of children in China find?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000458.answer_short: In 1,700 child autopsies in Keshan Province, China, 35% of those dying of the selenium-deficiency Keshan Disease had lesions consistent with cystic fibrosis.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000459.subject: stem_cells
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000459.question: Does Wallach believe in stem cell therapy?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000459.answer_short: Wallach holds that essential nutrients, especially colloidal minerals, will always outperform stem cells and other medical technology for preventing and reversing disease.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000460.subject: stem_cells
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000460.question: Do stem cell injections cure arthritis?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000460.answer_short: Wallach says mainstream medicine offers only stem cell injections and joint replacement for arthritis, while he holds that nutrition can prevent and reverse it.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000461.subject: stem_cells
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000461.question: What is a stem cell?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000461.answer_short: A stem cell is a self-renewing cell that can divide to make identical copies of itself or daughter cells with different developmental potentials.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000462.subject: mediterranean_diet
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000462.question: Is 'just follow the Mediterranean diet' good nutrition advice?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000462.answer_short: Wallach calls 'just follow the Mediterranean diet' an empty catch phrase reflecting little real understanding of nutrition.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000297.subject: gmo_foods
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000297.question: What does Wallach think of GMO foods?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000297.answer_short: Wallach calls genetically engineered crops "Frankenstein Food" and argues that manipulating genes without supplying the body's basic essential nutrients is a faulty, greedy premise.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000298.subject: ginger
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000298.question: Does ginger help with motion sickness?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000298.answer_short: Dr. Wallach lists ginger among the herbs that are useful for preventing motion sickness such as carsickness, seasickness, and air sickness.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000299.subject: emory_university
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000299.question: What did Dr. Wallach do at Emory University?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000299.answer_short: Wallach worked as a comparative pathologist at Emory University's Yerkes Regional Primate Research Center in Atlanta, a center administered by Emory and funded by the NIH and NASA, across the street from the CDC.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000300.subject: honey
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000300.question: Can honey cause hyperactivity in kids?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000300.answer_short: Wallach recounts a dyslexic child who followed the Feingold Diet except for honey and reacted so severely he was found on top of a 40-foot dome.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000301.subject: nobel_prize_nomination
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000301.question: Was Dr. Wallach nominated for a Nobel Prize?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000301.answer_short: In 1990 the Association of Eclectic Physicians forwarded a nomination to the Nobel Committee in Stockholm, nominating Wallach for the 1991 Nobel Prize in Medicine for his work linking cystic fibrosis to a maternal selenium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000302.subject: nobel_prize_nomination
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000302.question: How did Wallach react to his Nobel Prize nomination?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000302.answer_short: Wallach calls the 1991 Nobel nomination the pinnacle of his scientific career, but says it stirred jealous rage from many conventional and alternative-medicine doctors who resented that a maverick was so honored.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000303.subject: msg
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000303.question: Can MSG feel like a heart attack?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000303.answer_short: Wallach says that in people sensitive to MSG, eating it (the 'Chinese restaurant syndrome') can trigger sudden palpitations alarming enough to be mistaken for a heart attack -- a real food-allergy reaction that passes quickly. He counts MSG among the food allergens sensitive people should pin down (with his pulse test) and then avoid.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000304.subject: twenty_thousand_autopsies
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000304.question: What did Wallach's autopsies conclude?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000304.answer_short: Wallach's autopsies led him to conclude that every animal and every human dying of natural causes dies of a nutritional deficiency disease.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000305.subject: twenty_thousand_autopsies
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000305.question: Why don't doctors find nutritional deficiencies at autopsy?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000305.answer_short: Wallach says only about 5% of hospital deaths are autopsied (to limit malpractice data), and pathologists never record the nutritional deficiency behind the disease.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000306.subject: ma_lan
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000306.question: How did Dr. Wallach meet his wife?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000306.answer_short: Wallach met Ma Lan at the Jones Medical Library, courted her through fishing and sailing, and married her on Valentine's Day, 1987.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000307.subject: ma_lan
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000307.question: How did Ma Lan survive the Chinese Cultural Revolution?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000307.answer_short: Arrested as an academic and sent to forced labor in the rice fields, Ma Lan kept herself alive by adding river grass and mud to her meals.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000308.subject: ma_lan
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000308.question: Was Ma Lan a surgeon?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000308.answer_short: As a microsurgeon Ma Lan achieved a 95 percent success rate repairing arteries and veins as thin as a human hair, versus the typical 65 percent.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000309.subject: ma_lan
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000309.question: Why did Ma Lan eat fish bones?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000309.answer_short: Ma Lan ate fish bones and simmered bones in vinegar to leach out calcium, magnesium, manganese, boron, copper, and sulfur, which is how the dairy-free Chinese get their calcium.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000310.subject: colonics
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000310.question: Why do colonics during a candida or parasite cleanse?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000310.answer_short: Wallach uses colonics (with liver flushes), especially in the first two weeks of therapy, to detoxify the toxins produced as organisms die off during treatment.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000311.subject: colonics
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000311.question: Can you use an enema to restore acidophilus or good bacteria?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000311.answer_short: Wallach says reimplanting Lactobacillus acidophilus is useful in any Candida program, using a retention enema of 4 ounces of warm water containing 10 billion organisms (twenty 500,000-organism capsules).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000312.subject: shark_cartilage
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000312.question: How does shark cartilage fight cancer?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000312.answer_short: Wallach says shark cartilage contains angiostatin and endostatin, which stop the new capillaries a metastatic tumor needs to feed itself — an effect he says Harvard and Yale proved over 25 years of research.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000313.subject: shark_cartilage
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000313.question: How much shark cartilage does Wallach recommend for cancer?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000313.answer_short: Wallach says to start shark cartilage at 70 grams per day if you have cancer; he claims it shrinks metastases, reduces pain, and can make a growth smaller than a grape disappear.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000314.subject: shark_cartilage
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000314.question: Why does mainstream medicine call shark cartilage quackery?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000314.answer_short: Wallach says orthodox medicine dismissed shark cartilage — used by the Chinese for 5,000 years against cancer — as quackery, but now that angiostatin and endostatin can be patented, the same idea is rebranded as profitable 'science.'

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000315.subject: ginkgo
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000315.question: Is ginkgo good for angina?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000315.answer_short: Wallach says ginkgo and English hawthorn are specific for relieving angina by increasing blood flow through the coronary arteries.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000316.subject: ginkgo
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000316.question: Does ginkgo help memory?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000316.answer_short: Wallach lists ginkgo among the useful herbs in his treatment of dementia and memory loss.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000317.subject: ginkgo
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000317.question: Is ginkgo good for circulation?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000317.answer_short: Wallach includes ginkgo among the herbs he recommends for poor circulation, marked by cold hands and feet and numb, tingling fingers and toes.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000075.subject: sucralose
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000075.question: Is Splenda safe to use?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000075.answer_short: Wallach says that despite public controversy, sugar substitutes like Splenda are “considered” safe when used in moderation and have been used for years, and Splenda can replace sugar teaspoon for teaspoon in baking.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000076.subject: sucralose
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000076.question: Is Splenda natural or artificial?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000076.answer_short: Wallach classifies Splenda (Sucralose) as a natural substance extracted from sugar cane, unlike the man-made sweeteners aspartame and saccharin.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000077.subject: sucralose
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000077.question: When did Splenda become the most popular sweetener?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000077.answer_short: Wallach notes that during 2004 Splenda became the number one blended sweetener in the U.S., outselling every other brand of faux and real sugar.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000078.subject: high_fructose_corn_syrup
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000078.question: Why is high fructose corn syrup in everything?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000078.answer_short: Because it is cheaper, sweeter, and easier to handle than granulated sugar, so manufacturers put it in nearly every processed food, replacing more nutritious ingredients.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000079.subject: yogurt
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000079.question: Is low-fat or fat-free yogurt healthy?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000079.answer_short: Wallach's warning is specifically about LOW-FAT and 98% fat-free yogurt, which he says are 'loaded with sugar' -- not about yogurt itself. Elsewhere he counts whole-milk, live, and Greek yogurt among the staples of the longest-lived peoples (the Hunza and the Greek island of Symi), so full-fat yogurt is fine; it is the sugar-heavy reduced-fat versions he says to avoid.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000080.subject: microwaving_food
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000080.question: How does a microwave oven cook food?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000080.answer_short: Wallach simply describes the mechanism, without judging microwaves good or bad: the oven bombards food with ultra-short microwaves that make its water molecules vibrate millions of times per second, and the friction produces heat that cooks the food 'from the inside out.'

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000081.subject: microwaving_food
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000081.question: When were microwave ovens first sold?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000081.answer_short: Wallach says the first microwave ovens were marketed in the United States in 1947, though early sales were far lower than hoped.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000082.subject: keto_diet
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000082.question: What does Dr. Wallach think of the keto or low-carb diet?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000082.answer_short: Wallach favors low-carb, low-glycemic diets and counts his own See Food Diet -- his low-carb plan built around supplementing all 90 essential nutrients to kill cravings -- among them, but insists mineral intake matters far more than the exact ratio of carbs, fat, and protein, because he blames obesity on mineral deficiency, not carbohydrates.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000083.subject: low_carb_diet
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000083.question: Are low-carb diets the answer to obesity?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000083.answer_short: No -- Wallach grants low-carb diets can speed weight loss, but warns that if cutting carbs is your 'sole consideration ... you are in for a rude awakening': if low-carb were really the answer to obesity, we wouldn't be facing a projected 40% obesity rate. The rude awakening is that obesity's real root cause is mineral deficiency -- the cravings and binge-eating a mineral-starved body drives -- not carbohydrates. So cutting carbs alone can't solve it.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000084.subject: low_carb_diet
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000084.question: Are low-carb diets dangerous?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000084.answer_short: Low-carb weight loss can bring pitfalls like heart attacks, kidney stones, osteoporosis and stroke; Wallach says you must guard against mineral deficiencies and the free-radical damage from burning body fat.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000085.subject: low_carb_diet
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000085.question: Do low-carb diets create free radicals?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000085.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says burning body fat, like burning any fuel, produces free radicals and other harmful byproducts that must be countered with an antioxidant plan.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000086.subject: low_carb_diet
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000086.question: What is a low-carb diet?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000086.answer_short: A low-carb diet limits the amount and type of carbohydrates to steady blood sugar and lower glucose and insulin levels, reducing bouts of ravenous hunger.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000087.subject: grilled_bbq_meat
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000087.question: Does grilled or charred meat cause cancer?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000087.answer_short: Wallach says heterocyclic amines — free radicals formed in well-done meat and burnt animal fat — can raise the risk of breast, prostate, and colon cancer by as much as 462 percent compared with meat cooked medium-rare; it is the burning, not the meat, that harms you.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000088.subject: dialysis
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000088.question: Who invented the dialysis machine?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000088.answer_short: Wallach credits Dr. Willem Kolff, a Dutch physician, with developing the "artificial kidney" or dialysis machine, first employed in the United States, which cleanses metabolic wastes from the blood through a cellulose membrane.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000089.subject: dialysis
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000089.question: What is dialysis?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000089.answer_short: Wallach defines dialysis as a separation process in which inorganic colloids are too large to cross a semi-permeable membrane while dissolved salt, starch and sugar pass through as individual atoms or small molecules.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000091.subject: noni_juice
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000091.question: Is noni an antioxidant?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000091.answer_short: Yes, Wallach lists noni among the fruits that contain antioxidants in substantial quantities.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000093.subject: keto_diet
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000093.question: How does the keto or low-carb diet work?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000093.answer_short: Carbohydrates are cut to about twenty grams a day, with unlimited meat and fat, to lower glucose and insulin and push the body into ketosis so it burns fat for energy instead of carbohydrates.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000094.subject: keto_diet
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000094.question: Is the keto or low-carb diet dangerous?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000094.answer_short: An unsupplemented high-protein low-carb diet forgets the minerals and can increase the risk of kidney stones, which is why Wallach insists on mineral supplementation alongside it.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000467.subject: high_fructose_corn_syrup
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000467.question: Why do I crave soda and soft drinks?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000467.answer_short: Wallach says craving high-fructose-corn-syrup soft drinks first (and water last) is a sign of chromium and vanadium deficiency, which drives intense thirst and carbohydrate hunger.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000468.subject: high_fructose_corn_syrup
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000468.question: What is high fructose corn syrup?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000468.answer_short: It is a manufactured sweetener made from corn, sugar beet, and sugar cane, built from glucose and fructose (levulose), the sweetest of the natural sugars.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000469.subject: intermittent_fasting
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000469.question: Does intermittent fasting help you live longer?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000469.answer_short: Wallach cites a 1940s Carlson and Holzol study in which rats fasted every other, third, or fourth day extended their maximum life span 20 to 30%, from 800 to 1,000-1,100 days.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000470.subject: intermittent_fasting
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000470.question: Does fasting every other day extend lifespan?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000470.answer_short: Wallach cites Dr. Charles Goodrick's study in which rats fasted every other day extended maximum life span from 875 to 1,295 days.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000472.subject: twenty_thousand_autopsies
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000472.question: Why did Wallach start doing autopsies?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000472.answer_short: An NIH-funded project set out to see whether pollution caused deaths in zoo animals and humans; the autopsies pointed instead to nutritional deficiency.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000473.subject: stem_cells
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000473.question: Who kept chicken heart cells alive for 34 years?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000473.answer_short: Dr. Alexis Carrel grew fibroblast 'stem cells' from chicken hearts that kept multiplying for 34 years, giving rise to the idea of cellular immortality.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000475.subject: ma_lan
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000475.question: Who is Dr. Ma Lan?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000475.answer_short: Dr. Ma Lan is Dr. Joel Wallach's wife and co-author, a Chinese-trained MD and microsurgeon educated at Beijing Medical University.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000476.subject: noni_juice
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000476.question: What is the ORAC value of noni juice?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000476.answer_short: Wallach's ORAC table in Immortality lists noni juice at an ORAC value of 398 per serving.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000477.subject: mediterranean_diet
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000477.question: Is the Mediterranean diet actually healthy?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000477.answer_short: In Immortality, Wallach calls the classical Mediterranean diet 'legendary for its health benefits' and points to the long-lived Greek island of Symi as a success story.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000401.subject: honey
WAL-CLM-RARE-000401.question: Is honey bad for you?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000401.answer_short: Wallach treats honey as a sugar to avoid - sugar loads flush minerals out of the body in sweat and urine by 300% for 12 hours, so no supplement can keep up.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000402.subject: mediterranean_diet
WAL-CLM-RARE-000402.question: What does Dr. Wallach think of the Mediterranean diet?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000402.answer_short: Wallach says the Mediterranean diet, like every other named diet, makes no difference unless you also supplement all 90 essential nutrients daily.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000519.subject: msg
WAL-CLM-LETS-000519.question: What is Chinese restaurant syndrome?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000519.answer_short: Wallach calls it a classic food allergy to MSG: in sensitive people any contact with MSG triggers heart palpitations or a racing heartbeat (tachycardia).

WAL-CLM-LETS-000520.subject: msg
WAL-CLM-LETS-000520.question: How do you know if you're allergic to MSG?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000520.answer_short: Wallach points to the home pulse test — contact with MSG makes an allergic person's heart rate climb, MSG being the extreme example of this reaction.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000521.subject: colonics
WAL-CLM-LETS-000521.question: What is colonic irrigation used for?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000521.answer_short: Wallach lists colonic irrigation as a form of hydrotherapy, used for constipation and to detoxify patients being treated for any chronic disease or liver ailment (except infectious hepatitis).

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000095.subject: see_food_diet
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000095.question: What is Dr. Wallach's See Food Diet?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000095.answer_short: The See Food Diet is Dr. Wallach's own low-carb, low-glycemic weight-loss plan. What sets it apart, he says, is that it targets the real root cause of obesity -- mineral deficiency -- so the cravings, pica, and binge-eating that sink other diets disappear once the body is saturated with the essential minerals. (The name is Wallach's pun on 'see food and eat it.')
